note: Triennial election of the Strabane rural district councillors, 1939. Nominations were received by Mr. James L. Rankin, returning officer, from 10 to 18 April 1939. Every division was settled at the nominations: the only double nomination, Loughash, ended when the retiring member John Conway withdrew on 25 April, and 'There will be no contests in connection with Strabane Rural Council elections' (Derry Journal, 26 April 1939, p. 3). No nomination was received for Glenmoran, whose retiring member, Thomas Christy, was deemed re-elected (see the division's note). No poll was held; the Tyrone polling day for 1939 is not confirmed by any page read and the folder date is provisional. division inferred from the 3 June 1936 return (Thomas Christy, printed for 'Glenmorning'; Derry Journal, 6 May 1936, p. 8); the Strabane Chronicle, 10 June 1939, p. 1 names the member as sitting in the new term (he presided as vice-chairman at the annual meeting of the Strabane Board of Guardians, whose rural members were the rural district councillors, on 6 June 1939), and on 20 October 1939 counsel described him as 'a member of Strabane Rural Council' (Strabane Chronicle, 21 October 1939, p. 1). No nomination was received for Glenmoran; the retiring member was deemed re-elected. He had sat for the division since at least 1930. No co-option or by-election for Glenmoran was reported in 1939. Deemed re-elected (no nomination).
